claims.explanation: Carmofur's antiproliferative selectivity is best explained by its inhibition of acid ceramidase (ASAH1), which is overexpressed in many tumors and whose inhibition raises proapoptotic ceramide; lines with high ASAH1 expression and intact ceramide-driven apoptosis are therefore most sensitive. Because carmofur is a cysteine-reactive, thiol-targeting drug, sensitivity is also favored by low antioxidant capacity (e.g., NFE2L2/KEAP1 pathway alterations) and by loss of DNA-repair/apoptotic brakes such as TP53, while high expression of drug efflux or antioxidant programs protects.

features.basis: carmofur is a potent acid ceramidase inhibitor and this activity is essential to its antiproliferative effect
TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set, consistent with loss of apoptotic brakes enhancing ceramide/oxidative killing
NFE2L2-mutant squamous lines (TE6, KYSE70, HEC265) are among the most killed, suggesting oxidative-stress vulnerability
KEAP1 mutation in sensitive HEC265 implies impaired antioxidant response and greater ROS-mediated killing
SMARCA4-mutant lines are enriched in the sensitive group, possibly through chromatin-driven dependency on ceramide/redox homeostasis
ARID1A-mutant lines (JHUEM2, OVK18, KYSE70, HEC265, KU1919) are overrepresented among sensitive lines
KMT2C-mutant lines (T3M4, FTC238, OVK18) appear in the sensitive set
KMT2D-mutant lines (KYSE270, JHUEM2, OVK18, HEC265, KU1919) are enriched among sensitive lines
BRAF-mutant lines (AM38, HEC265, BCPAP, 8305C) are among the most killed
PTEN loss in several sensitive lines may increase ceramide-dependent apoptosis and PI3K-driven proliferation
CTNNB1-mutant lines (JHUEM2, U2OS, SW1573, HEC265) are enriched in the sensitive group
high efflux pump expression would reduce intracellular carmofur and its active metabolites
